notes:
I can't give you the Jeremiah 31 notes yet, because I wasn't able to read any sources.

I tried to open the Enduring Word, Precept Austin and BibleHub commentary pages for Jeremiah 31 directly, using addresses I typed in. The tool refused them because a page has to come up in a search result before it can be opened. When I then ran the searches to find those pages, the tool said I had used up my searches for this turn, so no results came back.

So I haven't read anything from Enduring Word, BibleHub, StudyLight, Precept Austin, the denominational sites, NET Bible, Bible Odyssey, or the Catholic and Orthodox sites. Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. That means anything I wrote now would be unsourced, so I've left the notes out rather than guess.

If you ask me to continue in a new message, I'll start again with searches and then read the pages they find, roughly in this order:
1. **Traditional reading:** Enduring Word's Jeremiah 31 page, Precept Austin's Jeremiah 31 commentary, and the BibleHub/StudyLight pages for Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary.
2. **Where Protestants differ:** mainly vv. 31–34, the "new covenant." That covers Reformed vs. Baptist views of who the covenant is made with (Ligonier, TGC, Monergism, Desiring God, GTY), dispensational readings about Israel and the church (Bible.org, GotQuestions), Wesley's notes and Lutheran writing (LCMS, 1517). I'd also check vv. 35–37 on whether Israel continues as a nation.
3. **Other views:** NET Bible notes on v. 22 ("a woman will shelter a man") and v. 15 (Rachel weeping, which Matthew quotes). Then Catholic and Orthodox readings of v. 22 and vv. 31–34 (New Advent, Catholic.com, OCA), and any well-known popular modern teaching tied to vv. 31–34, such as hyper-grace.

Each point will come with the page link, in the "v. 4: …" format you asked for.
